# FVM

> Install Flutter SDKs, select a version per project, and run Flutter with its bundled Dart.

These docs describe mrgnhnt96/fvm, a standalone manager separate from the pub.dev package named fvm. Start with Getting Started. `fvm install stable` downloads the current stable release; `fvm use stable` saves its concrete version in `.fvmrc`. Commit `.fvmrc`, ignore `.fvm/`, and point the editor at `.fvm/flutter_sdk`.

## Documentation

- [Getting Started](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mrgnhnt96/fvm/main/apps/docs/content/index.md): Install FVM, choose Flutter for your project, and run your app.
- [Managing Versions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mrgnhnt96/fvm/main/apps/docs/content/versions.md): Select Flutter with project pins, defaults, channels, and aliases.
- [Commands](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mrgnhnt96/fvm/main/apps/docs/content/commands.md): Reference for all FVM commands and their options.
- [Updating](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mrgnhnt96/fvm/main/apps/docs/content/updating.md): Update FVM and choose when projects move to a newer Flutter SDK.
- [CI](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mrgnhnt96/fvm/main/apps/docs/content/ci.md): Install your project’s Flutter version and run checks in CI.
- [Troubleshooting](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mrgnhnt96/fvm/main/apps/docs/content/troubleshooting.md): Fix missing commands, incorrect SDK selection, and editor setup.
